summary: This note surveys several mobility and transportation startups launched in 2023-2024 that aim to make urban transport cleaner, smarter and more inclusive. It covers electric vehicles, autonomous driving software, freight logistics, last-mile delivery, accessibility, flying cars and eVTOL air mobility. It also notes a trend of startups partnering with established corporations.
one_line: Profile of 2023-2024 mobility startups spanning EVs, autonomy, freight, last-mile delivery, accessibility and urban air mobility.
key_facts: ElectraZoom, founded by Sarah Vandiver in September 2023, makes compact, high-performance zero-emissions EVs for city dwellers with AI-based predictive maintenance and optimized battery life.
On October 14th, Sarah Vandiver revealed a pilot 'EV-share' initiative, similar to bike-sharing schemes.
AutonoMe Tech, started in October 2023 by MIT graduates led by Dr. Juan Martinez, has a proprietary software platform that integrates with existing vehicles for autonomous driving.
AutonoMe Tech is currently conducting road tests in Boston.
FreightWise Technologies, launched in November 2023 by Anika Bhatnagar, uses IoT and machine learning to optimize cargo routes, predict delays and improve load management.
Anika Bhatnagar spoke about waste in logistics, from fuel consumption to idling in traffic, in an interview on November 20th.
SwiftlyDrop, founded in December 2023 by college friends Gregor Huang and Maia Roberts, builds a fleet of autonomous delivery drones and robots for last-mile delivery.
WheelEasy, a March 2024 startup by Paralympian Lilly Tran, builds platforms and vehicles designed to be universally accessible to people with disabilities.

SkyLink Dynamics, co-founded by aerospace engineers Max Peterson and Zoe Li, partnered with a major automotive company to integrate electric propulsion for short-range air travel into future flying cars.
Max Peterson spoke about the SkyLink Dynamics partnership at an online summit held on February 23rd.
AeroHive, led by CEO Ravi Shah since January 2024, proposes a fleet of eVTOL vehicles for urban air mobility, aiming to cut commutes from hours to minutes.
Ravi Shah says AeroHive wants affordable, on-demand air travel accessible to all city residents, not only the affluent.
